component.name: Button
component.description: Triggers an action. Four variants that name an absolute visual weight, not a rank (accent brand-fill, neutral bordered, transparent ghost, danger error-fill) — the container decides which weight an action gets (ADR-024). Three sizes, optional leading and/or trailing icon, icon-only shapes. Fully keyboard-accessible via the native button element.

when: The single most important action in a decision region — form or dialog footer, hero (variant=accent, at most one per region)
Everyday or supporting actions, and the lead action inside a card or other repeated item (variant=neutral — the default)
A low-weight action inline with content, e.g. 'Show more' under an accordion or Close in a panel (variant=transparent)
A destructive or irreversible action — delete, remove, deactivate (variant=danger, paired with a neutral Cancel)
Triggering a form submit, modal open, or in-page state change

patterns.name: form-actions
patterns.description: Decision-region footer: one accent confirm with a neutral cancel.

patterns.name: destructive-confirm
patterns.description: Confirming a destructive action: danger replaces accent; cancel stays neutral.

patterns.name: card-actions
patterns.description: Actions inside a card or other repeated item: the lead action is neutral, the second transparent. Never accent — N cards would mean N primaries.
patterns.tree: Card > Stack(gap=md) > [Heading, Text, Inline(gap=sm) > [Button(variant=neutral, size=sm), Button(variant=transparent, size=sm)]]

patterns.name: hero-cta
patterns.description: A single large accent Button below a Heading and Text block.

antiPatterns.scenario: Using accent or neutral for a destructive action
antiPatterns.reason: Making delete look like the page's main call to action trains users to click it. Weight alone does not signal consequence.
antiPatterns.alternative: Use variant=danger, paired with a neutral Cancel (pattern destructive-confirm).

antiPatterns.scenario: More than one accent Button in the same decision region, or any accent Button inside a repeated item (card, list row, carousel slide)
antiPatterns.reason: Variants are absolute weights, not ranks. Rank comes from the container: a card's lead action is not the page's lead action, and N repeated cards would render N competing primaries.
antiPatterns.alternative: Keep accent for the one action that region exists to decide; use neutral for the card's lead action and transparent for its secondary one (pattern card-actions).

antiPatterns.scenario: Using a transparent or neutral icon button over an image or video thumbnail without a contrast treatment
antiPatterns.reason: Both have no opaque background, so the glyph's contrast depends on whatever pixels are underneath and can drop to near zero on a light or busy photo. Hover tints do not fix it: there is no hover on touch, and contrast is judged at rest.
antiPatterns.alternative: The media-overlay treatment is owned by the parent molecule (ADR-009 rule 3): CardVertical's Favorite and Menu render variant=transparent with an icon.on-media glyph plus icon.on-media.halo drop-shadow. Reuse those parts rather than re-styling Button.

antiPatterns.scenario: Using Button for navigation that produces a URL
antiPatterns.reason: Produces a <button> element; links that change the URL should be <a> elements for correct semantics and accessibility.
antiPatterns.alternative: Use an anchor tag styled to match, passing className to override

antiPatterns.scenario: Passing raw design values via the style prop
antiPatterns.reason: Breaks token alignment and prevents theme switching from working.
antiPatterns.alternative: Use the variant and size props; extend via className if needed

antiPatterns.scenario: Building a new native-button-wrapping component without defaulting the type attribute
antiPatterns.reason: An unset <button> type defaults to "submit" inside a <form>; Button, Chip, and ButtonArrow all default to type="button" internally for exactly this reason — a new component would silently submit forms without it.
antiPatterns.alternative: Default type to "button" internally (as Button does) and let consumers opt in to type="submit" explicitly.

purpose.accent: Highest weight. Brand fill with inverted text. The one action a decision region exists for (form/dialog footer, hero). Never inside a repeated item.
purpose.neutral: Default. Bordered, neutral text. Everyday and supporting actions; the lead action inside a card or other repeated item.
purpose.transparent: Lowest weight. Ghost button: no background or border at rest, interactive text color, standard size padding, and a subtle fill on hover (button.transparent.hover). Low-weight actions such as 'Show more' or Close. Its label sits inset from the content edge by the size padding — accepted, no negative-margin bleed (ADR-024 amendment 2026-10-06).
purpose.danger: Destructive or irreversible actions. Error fill with inverted text. Pair with a neutral Cancel.

purpose.sm: 32px height. Dense UI: table rows, inline actions, toolbars.
purpose.md: 40px height. Default for most page contexts.
purpose.lg: 48px height. Hero sections, prominent CTAs, touch-optimised flows.

purpose.square: Icon-only button with rounded-sm corners. Use in toolbars, table rows, and inline action groups. Requires the icon prop and an aria-label.
purpose.round: Icon-only button with full circular border-radius. Use for floating actions or avatar-adjacent controls. Requires the icon prop and an aria-label.

states.description: Darker fill (accent, danger) or subtle fill (neutral, transparent) on pointer hover.

Momentary press feedback while the pointer or Space key is held (CSS :active): one step darker fill than hover; neutral and transparent also darken their text one step to hold AA on the stronger fill. Not a toggle — a persistent on/off is aria-pressed, which Button does not have (see Chip).
Muted background and text; cursor not-allowed; interaction blocked natively.

ariaAttributes: aria-label (set on icon-only buttons via shape to provide an accessible name; flows through ...rest)
disabled (native HTML attribute via disabled prop, not aria-disabled)

keyboardInteractions.action: Moves focus to the next focusable element

accessibility.notes: Uses a native <button> element. The disabled prop sets the HTML disabled attribute, which natively prevents click events and removes the element from the tab order.
